topic: Capstone Demonstration, Portfolio, UX Case Study, and Future Roadmap
learningObjectives: Understand how to present a full-stack capstone project clearly.
Explain the architecture and technical decisions behind a project.
Create a concise UX case study that communicates the design process.
Identify improvements and future development opportunities.

activities.title: Build the Project Story
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages in the order you would use to present your capstone project.

content.concept: A strong project presentation tells a clear story. Start with the problem and target users, explain the solution and key features, show the UX and technical design process, demonstrate the implementation and testing, present the final result, and finish with realistic future improvements.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Explain Your Technical Architecture
activities.instruction: Select the components that belong in a clear technical architecture explanation.

content.concept: A technical architecture explains how the major parts of an application communicate. A typical full-stack application has users interacting with a frontend, which communicates with a backend API. The backend contains business logic and communicates with a database and external services. Deployment infrastructure hosts and connects these components in production.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Create a UX Case Study
activities.instruction: Build a case study that explains how your design decisions were made.

content.concept: A UX case study documents the reasoning behind a product's design. It should explain the original problem, target users, research findings, user flows and wireframes, important design decisions and iterations, the prototype or implemented interface, and the validation performed through usability and accessibility testing. The focus should be on decisions and evidence rather than simply displaying final screens.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Prepare the Final Project Review
activities.instruction: Explore the evidence that should support a professional capstone demonstration.

content.concept: A professional capstone review should demonstrate more than a working application. Show the working product, explain the architecture, provide evidence of testing, communicate the UX design process, describe deployment and configuration, provide useful documentation, and identify realistic future improvements. Together, these demonstrate both implementation ability and engineering decision-making.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Demonstrate the main user journey and important features working in the application.
Show how the frontend, backend, database, authentication, and external services are connected.
Present relevant unit, integration, end-to-end, accessibility, security, or performance testing evidence.
Explain the user problem, research, flows, design decisions, iterations, and validation.
Explain where the application is deployed and how environment variables, services, and production configuration are handled.
Provide setup instructions, architecture notes, API information, and other information needed to understand or maintain the project.
Identify practical improvements, additional features, scalability work, or technical enhancements for future versions.
